data.title: IAG Earnings Call Highlights Strong Revenue and Cash Generation
data.description:
International Consolidated Airlines Group, S.A. ((ICAGY)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

International Airlines Group delivered a predominantly positive earnings call, highlighting record revenue, strong yields, industry-leading margins, robust bookings, improving loyalty earnings and lower net debt. These gains outweighed lower year-on-year profit, higher fuel and disruption costs, foreign-exchange pressure, intense competition and delayed aircraft deliveries.

Record Revenue and Solid Profitability

IAG reported third-quarter revenue growth of 4.5% to a record level, with yields rising across all markets. Operating profit reached €1.726 billion, producing a 17.7% margin, while the first-nine-month operating margin was 13.5%.

Broad-Based Revenue Growth

Passenger revenue increased by €334 million, led by strong yields, particularly on long-haul routes. Cargo revenue rose €60 million as better pricing offset lower volumes, while other revenue grew €81 million through IAG Loyalty and higher Iberia Maintenance activity.

Passenger Unit Revenue Strength

Passenger unit revenue increased 4.1%, or 4.3% at constant currency, despite a 0.2% capacity decline. The North Atlantic was the standout region, with unit revenue up 11% on broadly unchanged capacity.

Regional Markets Remained Resilient

Latin America unit revenue rose 2.3%, or 3.4% at constant currency, as capacity expanded 5.4%. Africa, the Middle East and South Asia delivered a 13.2% unit-revenue increase with capacity down 19%, while Asia Pacific grew 3.8% on 9.3% higher capacity.

British Airways Led the Portfolio

British Airways generated £600 million of operating profit at a 14.4% margin, with unit revenue up 5.8%. Business revenue increased about 14% year over year in the quarter, supported by particularly strong North Atlantic performance.

All Airlines Posted Double-Digit Margins

Aer Lingus delivered €142 million of operating profit at a 17.4% margin, while Iberia produced €452 million at 19.6%. Vueling reported €257 million at a group-leading 23.8% margin, meaning every IAG airline achieved a double-digit quarterly margin.

IAG Loyalty Continued Its Expansion

IAG Loyalty operating profit increased 8% in the quarter, with underlying pre-HMRC profit rising £20 million to £171 million. The core loyalty business grew 20%, reinforcing its role as an increasingly important source of earnings diversification.

Cost Transformation Limited Inflation

Reported nonfuel unit costs rose 3.4%, but underlying nonfuel CASK increased only about 0.5% after adjusting for capacity, third-party maintenance, disruption and foreign exchange. Management pointed to tighter recruitment and stronger controls over suppliers, technology, artificial intelligence and discretionary spending.

Vueling Improved Costs and Customer Scores

Vueling’s transformation program, covering suppliers, specifications and technology, supported its cost performance. Its Net Promoter Score increased four points, while Spanish domestic capacity grew 7.3% and the airline retained a strong market position.

Debt Fell as Cash Generation Strengthened

Net debt declined to €4.2 billion from €4.7 billion at the half year and €5.9 billion at the end of the previous year. Net leverage fell 0.6 times, gross leverage stood at 1.9 times, and management expects 2026 free cash flow of about €3 billion.

Shareholder Returns Increased

IAG raised its interim dividend per share by 10% and continued its €1.5 billion share buyback program. Management also confirmed that the 2026 buyback program is being completed, underscoring confidence in the group’s balance sheet and cash generation.

Demand and Bookings Stayed Strong

The group was 85% booked for expected fourth-quarter demand, while bookings for the first quarter of 2027 were described as very strong. Passenger RASK was improving above third-quarter levels, with positive or resilient trends across the North Atlantic, Iberia, Latin America, Europe and domestic markets.

Corporate Travel Remained Robust

Corporate demand continued to perform well, led by technology and banking customers. British Airways reported strength among finance companies, technology firms and smaller businesses, along with healthy connecting traffic between the United States and India.

Fuel Recovery Made Progress

IAG expects to recover more than 80% of its full-year fuel costs, while British Airways is expected to recover over 100%. British Airways’ third-quarter fuel pass-through was about 75%, and management said pricing power remained strong in several markets.

Capacity and Fleet Plans Became More Disciplined

IAG reduced winter capacity in a measured effort to protect revenue and profitability. Full-year aircraft deliveries were cut to 12 from 16, while capital expenditure is now expected to be about €3.1 billion, below the previous €3.4 billion guidance.

Fleet and Product Investments Advanced

The group received its first Boeing 787-10 with GE engines in mid-October. British Airways’ new Club cabin retrofit was 82% complete at Heathrow, and the carrier aims to have Starlink installed on at least half of its long-haul fleet by year-end.

Investment Across the Airline Portfolio

IAG is continuing to invest in aircraft, customer initiatives and digital capabilities. Iberia plans cabin retrofits from 2027, Aer Lingus expects new business-class and premium-economy retrofits next year, and British Airways is planning a new First cabin on A380 and 777-9 aircraft from 2028.

Engine Business Set for Expansion

ITOCHU is investing in IAG Engine Tech after Iberia Maintenance won a LEAP engine license. The business plans to increase activity from about 200 engines annually to at least 350, backed by €400 million of investment and the recruitment of roughly 400 mechanics and engineers.

Aer Lingus Transformation Continued

Aer Lingus reported progress in head-office savings, digital revenue tools, supplier costs and the rollout of Starlink. One-third of senior managers had already left as part of the head-office cost-reduction program, reflecting the scale of the restructuring effort.

Funding and Hedging Remained Strong

IAG said it was not facing specific concerns in aircraft funding markets and was increasing the unencumbered share of its fleet. About 45% of 2027 fuel needs were hedged, with most protection linked to gas oil and jet fuel rather than Brent crude.

Operating Profit Declined Year Over Year

Third-quarter operating profit was €1.7 billion, down €327 million from the prior year’s record quarter. Operating profit before exceptional items for the first nine months fell 11% to €3.5 billion, showing that strong revenue did not fully offset higher costs.

Lower Profit and Adjusted Earnings

Profit after tax before exceptional items declined 12% to €2.4 billion in the first nine months. Adjusted earnings per share fell 9.2% to €0.154, with the lower profit only partly offset by the reduced share count created by the buyback program.

Fuel Costs Were a Major Headwind

Fuel costs increased €565 million in the third quarter as the Middle East conflict pushed jet fuel prices higher, although hedging provided some protection. Fuel unit costs jumped 30.7%, contributing to a 10.5% increase in total unit costs.

Nonfuel Expenses Also Increased

Nonfuel costs rose €163 million, with nonfuel unit costs up 3.4%. Employee unit costs increased 3%, supplier unit costs rose 2.9%, and ownership unit costs climbed 6.8%, adding pressure despite the group’s efficiency programs.

Operational Disruptions Raised Costs

Air traffic control outages, Heathrow baggage-system failures and unusually high Iberia engine costs added about 0.5 percentage points to nonfuel unit-cost growth. Lower-than-planned capacity contributed another 1.1 points, while greater third-party maintenance activity at Iberia added 1 point.

British Airways Faced Cost Pressure

British Airways’ nonfuel unit costs increased 5.1%, reflecting lower-than-planned capacity after repeated delays to the Middle East restart. Operational inefficiencies, NATS air traffic control outages and Heathrow baggage-system failures also weighed on the carrier’s performance.

Foreign Exchange Reduced Results

Foreign exchange was a €30 million net headwind in the third quarter because the weaker U.S. dollar reduced reported revenue. Management expects currency movements to remain a cost-side headwind in the fourth quarter, although they should provide support on the revenue side.

Middle East Disruption Limited Capacity

Third-quarter capacity was flat instead of the previously planned growth of about 1%, reflecting Middle East disruption, flight cancellations and U.K. air traffic control issues. IAG also expects some capacity to remain below original plans because aircraft redeployment from the region has been difficult.

Aircraft Deliveries Were Delayed

Expected 2026 deliveries were reduced to 12 from 16, with three Vueling Boeing 737s and one British Airways A321neo moving into 2027. The Boeing 777-9 is now expected in 2028, and management warned that further slippage could affect subsequent years.

Aer Lingus Faces Competitive Pressure

Aer Lingus expects a challenging competitive environment, with Ryanair announcing about 15% capacity growth for next summer. The North Atlantic market is also still absorbing a 50% capacity increase accumulated over recent years.

Vueling Saw Softer Leisure Demand

Leisure demand at Vueling was relatively soft through most of the summer, although trading improved from September. The airline nevertheless maintained its market position and continued to benefit from its transformation program.

European Competition Intensified

IAG described intra-European markets as highly competitive, with substantial capacity growth from rivals. The group reduced European capacity by 1.2% to protect profitability, prioritizing returns over volume in a crowded market.

Iberia Absorbed Engine Maintenance Costs

Iberia faced higher-than-expected engine maintenance challenges during the quarter. Airline-level nonfuel unit costs improved slightly by 0.3%, but unusually high engine-related expenses were identified as a one-off headwind.

Leverage Could Rise Seasonally

Management expects leverage to increase by year-end as seasonal booking patterns affect cash collection. The impact of seven aircraft deliveries expected in the following quarter will also increase capital expenditure and temporarily weigh on leverage.

2027 Capacity Growth Will Be Limited

IAG expects 2027 capacity growth to remain below mid-single digits, although the timing will depend partly on developments in the Middle East. The restrained plan reflects management’s focus on balancing demand, profitability and fleet availability.

Aer Lingus Margin Faced Seasonal Pressure

Aer Lingus produced a strong 17.4% margin in the seasonal quarter, but the result was lower than a year earlier. Management acknowledged the impact of increased competition while the airline continues to adapt its cost structure.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management maintained its expectation for a full-year operating margin of at least 12%, significant free cash flow and about €3 billion of free cash flow in 2026, while ruling out a negative free-cash-flow scenario in 2026 or 2027. Fuel recovery is expected to exceed 80% groupwide and 100% at British Airways, with 2027 capacity growth below mid-single digits.

The group expects passenger RASK to remain above third-quarter levels, while lower disruption should support nonfuel CASK in the fourth quarter and foreign exchange should remain mixed. IAG now expects 12 aircraft deliveries and about €3.1 billion of capital expenditure for the year, with roughly 45% of next year’s fuel needs hedged.

Overall, IAG’s call showed a business with strong pricing power, resilient demand and improving financial flexibility, even as profits declined from an exceptional prior-year comparison. Investors will be watching fuel, disruption, competition and fleet delays, but continued cash generation, shareholder returns and disciplined capacity planning leave the group on a constructive footing.

data.title: Power Corp. Earnings Call Highlights Strong Growth and Returns
data.description:
Power Corp Of Canada ((TSE:POW)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Power Corp.’s third-quarter call was strongly constructive, with broad earnings growth, record operating metrics, rising net asset value and substantial shareholder returns. Weakness in some NAV-based businesses, higher corporate costs, ChinaAMC’s asset decline and a still-material NAV discount were notable, but the positive developments outweighed the challenges.

Adjusted Earnings and EPS Growth

Power Corp. reported third-quarter adjusted net earnings of $964 million, up 12% from a year earlier. Adjusted earnings per share rose 13% to $1.53, supported by strong momentum at Great-West and IGM.

Great-West Delivers Strong Results

Great-West contributed $905 million to Power’s adjusted net earnings, a 7% year-over-year increase. Its base EPS rose 11% to $1.48, while base return on equity reached a record 19.4%, above its medium-term target for a third consecutive quarter.

Empower Maintains Operating Momentum

Empower’s base earnings increased 15% year over year on a constant-currency basis, with Retirement Services client assets reaching $2.15 trillion. Empower Wealth earnings climbed 28%, while its pretax base operating margin improved by 410 basis points.

IGM Reports a Record Quarter

IGM posted record third-quarter adjusted EPS of $1.51, up 19% year over year and ahead of its medium-term growth target of more than 9%. Wealth Management was a key contributor to the stronger result.

IGM Wealth Management Expands

IGM’s Wealth Management business grew 30% year over year, with assets under management and advisement rising 14% to $178 billion. The division recorded a third-quarter high for new client gross inflows, while net flows at IG Wealth and Mackenzie, including Northleaf, reached $3.4 billion.

IGM Boosts Returns and Investments

IGM returned more than $1 billion to shareholders during the first nine months through $585 million of buybacks and $421 million of dividends. It raised its Northleaf ownership to about 61%, while its Wealthsimple stake was valued at $2.9 billion.

Investment Fund Sales Improve

IGM investment fund net sales rose to $664 million from $407 million in the same quarter last year. The increase points to improving investor demand across its fund platform.

Rockefeller and Northleaf Grow

Rockefeller’s client assets increased 27% year over year to $236.5 billion. Northleaf’s client assets rose 10% to just under $38 billion, adding scale to Power’s alternative investment platform.

Wealthsimple Adds Clients and Assets

Wealthsimple’s assets under administration rose to $170 billion from $155 billion in the previous quarter, helped by about $11 billion in net flows. The platform added 200,000 clients and now serves approximately 4 million Canadians, while Power’s collective interest was valued at $5 billion net of carry.

NAV and Cash Position Strengthen

Power’s net asset value per share reached $113.28 at the end of the quarter, up 57% year over year, and stood at $120.20 as of the night before the call. Cash and equivalents totaled $1.9 billion, including $1.6 billion available after dividends receivable and payable, while public companies represented 90% of gross asset value.

Shareholder Returns Accelerate

Power returned $2.4 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks in the first nine months, compared with $1.5 billion a year earlier. Since 2020, total distributions through these channels have exceeded $13 billion.

Great-West Retains Capital Flexibility

Great-West repurchased nearly $1.3 billion of its shares year to date and held $2.8 billion in cash after accounting for a planned bond repayment. Power said it still intends to participate proportionately in Great-West’s additional $1.6 billion buyback program.

GBL Simplifies Its Portfolio

GBL has completed more than €5 billion of disposals involving listed companies and noncore assets. It returned €888 million through buybacks and dividends year to date and has set a 12-month goal of returning about €1 billion, without needing asset sales for liquidity.

Alternative Platforms Continue Scaling

Power’s alternative asset management platforms ended the quarter with $71.4 billion in assets under management. Sagard raised about C$1.4 billion during the quarter and nearly C$4 billion year to date, while increasing its economic interest in HalseyPoint to 60%.

Power Sustainable Plans Major Investment

Power Sustainable plans to invest and mobilize more than $10 billion in Canadian projects and companies over the next five years. Its infrastructure funds advanced new financing, capital recycling and renewable energy and storage opportunities across North America.

Management Emphasizes Active Ownership

Management described active ownership in strategy, capital allocation, leadership and risk management as a core value-creation tool. It is also focusing on artificial intelligence to help operating companies capture opportunities, building on earlier efforts in fintech and digitalization.

Proprietary Investments Produce Solid Returns

Power said returns on proprietary investments and co-investments supporting its alternative platforms exceeded 10% over the past one-, three- and five-year periods. The results reinforce the contribution of these investments beyond Power’s listed holdings.

NAV Discount Narrows

Power’s NAV discount narrowed to roughly 20% during the quarter, while NAV has grown at a 19% compound annual rate since 2020. Management said shareholder returns have materially outperformed both the S&P/TSX Financials Index and the broader S&P/TSX Composite across multiple time periods.

Some NAV Businesses Remain Challenged

GBL and Power Sustainable reported adjusted losses broadly in line with previous periods. These results highlight the earnings volatility that can accompany Power’s NAV-based and alternative businesses.

Sagard Earnings Face Investment Pressure

Sagard’s results were affected by lower earnings from investing activities, an investment loss and carried-interest expense linked to the rise in Wealthsimple’s value. These items weighed on reported earnings despite continued fundraising progress.

Corporate Costs Increase

Corporate operations and other activities produced a $107 million loss, including $61 million of operating expenses. Costs increased from the prior quarter because of higher performance-based compensation tied to strong operating results and Power’s higher share price.

ChinaAMC Assets Decline

ChinaAMC assets decreased 5% on a local-currency basis during the quarter. Management attributed the decline to weaker local markets rather than a broad deterioration across Power’s operating businesses.

Carried Interest Creates Volatility

Carried interest is recorded as an expense, creating an earnings drag when Wealthsimple’s value increases. Management said the net carry figure is difficult to forecast and can shift significantly, although current Wealthsimple share losses could eventually become a share of earnings.

Sagard Fee Earnings Remain Uneven

Market conditions and rate volatility continue to make fundraising, capital deployment and monetization difficult for Sagard. Although fee-related earnings were positive for two quarters, management cautioned that the measure will be volatile and will not be positive every quarter.

Discount Still Leaves Room for Improvement

Despite narrowing to about 20%, Power’s NAV discount remains material. Management said it is focused on growing NAV, increasing the dividend, simplifying the company and building more sustainable earnings.

Simplification Depends on Market Conditions

Potential transactions, including consolidating Wealthsimple ownership, would require willing buyers and sellers, sensible financing and clear benefits for shareholders. Management said such opportunities cannot be scheduled, while other possibilities include combining businesses or capabilities held in different parts of the group.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Management said Great-West and IGM are exceeding their adjusted EPS growth targets, supporting expected low- to mid-teen returns including dividends. Great-West plans another $1.6 billion buyback, while Sagard is targeting US$100 billion of assets over the next several years and expects sustainable fee-related earnings and margins to improve directionally toward 2027.

GBL aims to return about €1 billion through buybacks and dividends over the next 12 months, while Power continues to target a 10% return on proprietary investments. Power’s own buybacks are expected to begin with a base range similar to recent years, from a few hundred million dollars up to about $400 million, with further direction from Great-West’s program.

Power Corp.’s call showed a company benefiting from strong performance at Great-West and IGM, growing wealth platforms and a sharp rise in NAV. While alternative earnings, corporate expenses and the discount to NAV remain concerns, substantial cash generation, capital returns and long-term growth initiatives kept the overall message firmly positive.

data.title: Liquidity Services Earnings Call Signals Strong Fiscal Growth
data.description:
Liquidity Services ((LQDT)) has held its Q4 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Liquidity Services ended fiscal 2026 on a strongly positive note, reporting record GMV, higher profits, strong cash generation and broader buyer engagement. Management acknowledged softer vehicle pricing, retail inventory pressure, unchanged annual revenue and delayed Capital Asset Group projects, but described these issues as manageable while highlighting technology progress and the Invaluable acquisition.

Record GMV and Profitability

Liquidity Services increased fiscal 2026 GMV 5% to a record $1.645 billion. GAAP net income rose 33% to $37.3 million, adjusted EBITDA climbed 30% to $79.1 million and adjusted EPS advanced 27% to $1.63.

Strong Cash Position

Operating cash flow reached $58 million in fiscal 2026, while cash, equivalents and short-term investments totaled about $225 million at year-end. The company had no financial debt and spent $9.2 million on capital expenditures.

Fourth-Quarter Earnings Growth

Fourth-quarter GMV was $404 million and revenue was $106.4 million, while GAAP net income rose 52% to $11.9 million. Adjusted EBITDA increased 20% to $22.3 million, marking the 11th straight quarter of year-over-year growth.

Buyer and Transaction Engagement

Registered buyers grew nearly 8% to approximately 6.5 million. Fourth-quarter auction participants increased 24% to about 1.25 million, and completed transactions jumped 36% to roughly 365,000.

GovDeals Delivers Full-Year Growth

GovDeals full-year GMV increased 5% to $952.3 million, revenue grew 7% to $93.4 million and segment direct profit rose 9% to $88.6 million. Its direct-profit margin expanded to 94.8%, while the team signed more than 500 new accounts in the fourth quarter.

Marketplace and Real Estate Expansion

GovDeals completed notable sales, including fiber optic cable for $8.3 million and equipment transactions for Pennsylvania’s transportation department and the USPS. Bid4Assets also entered new jurisdictions through Milwaukee County foreclosure auctions, Louisiana sheriff contracts and additional Florida opportunities.

Registration and AI Cataloging

A progressive WSO2 registration experience lifted registrations 25% week over week, adding about 2,000 registrations in seven days. AssetPicks, Liquidity Services’ AI-enabled cataloging service, entered production beta with tools for both self-service and full-service sellers.

Retail Profitability Improves

Retail supply chain GMV increased 7% for the year to $447.2 million, while segment direct profit rose 21% to $90.4 million. The direct-profit margin expanded nearly 600 basis points to 28.5%, reaching 35% in the fourth quarter.

Retail Client and Consumer Momentum

One of the company’s five largest omnichannel retail clients increased quarterly GMV 65%, while its net recovery improved 22% sequentially. Managed third-party direct-to-consumer GMV rose 47%, and RetailRush GMV climbed 58% to about $1.6 million.

International Retail Expansion

An international ecommerce client produced a record GMV quarter, and Liquidity Services expanded the solution into more locations. Liquidation.com traffic increased 6% year over year, while truckload buyers grew 22%.

Capital Asset Group Profit Growth

Capital Asset Group revenue increased 16% for the year to $45.6 million, and segment direct profit rose 12% to $38.9 million. Fourth-quarter direct profit reached $10.3 million, the group’s highest quarterly result in a decade.

Heavy Equipment Gains Momentum

CAG heavy-equipment transactions increased 54% for the year, while assets sold rose 25%. In the fourth quarter, heavy equipment drove a 21% GMV increase and transactions grew 47%, supported by national fleet mandates.

Project Pipeline and Digital Demand

CAG completed projects involving Shell Energy, Occidental, Seagate Semiconductor Equipment, Agilent and Canon manufacturing equipment. Cross-listing selected assets generated about $2.5 million of additional GMV and lifted price per asset 24%, while AI-optimized pages increased views.

Machinio Builds Recurring Revenue

Machinio and software solutions revenue grew 10% to $21.7 million, and direct profit increased 8% to $19.8 million. Machinio surpassed 1,000 clients, expanding the company’s recurring subscription base and maintaining a direct-profit margin above 91%.

Technology and Analytics Advance

Liquidity Services launched progressive buyer registration, improved retail inventory ingestion and expanded automated reconciliation between marketplace and financial systems. Its CRM now receives daily data covering more than 23,000 records and 50 seller attributes, while analytics tools cut account-review preparation time by about 80%.

AI and Platform Infrastructure

The company continued investing in AI automation, analytics, identity management and software delivery. It modernized deployment with GitHub Actions and keyless AWS authentication, strengthening defenses against malicious storefront requests without disrupting legitimate customers.

Invaluable Acquisition Broadens Reach

Liquidity Services completed its $80 million cash acquisition of Invaluable after fiscal year-end. The deal adds fine art, antiques, jewelry and collectibles to the marketplace portfolio and expands the combined buyer base to approximately 10 million.

Path Toward Larger GMV and EBITDA

Management said Invaluable creates a path to more than $2 billion of consolidated GMV in fiscal 2027 and toward $2.5 billion over the near term. The chief executive also outlined a potential $2.5 billion GMV business with a $100 million EBITDA run rate.

Annual Revenue Holds Steady

Fiscal-year revenue was $477.9 million, essentially unchanged from the prior year. Management attributed the result to a continued shift toward higher-margin, asset-light consignment transactions.

Fourth-Quarter Revenue Declines

Consolidated fourth-quarter revenue declined 10% to $106.4 million because of product-mix and pricing-model changes in retail. The decline occurred despite improved retail direct-profit margins.

Retail Volume Softens

Fourth-quarter retail GMV fell 4% and revenue dropped 18% year over year. Management said profitability improved as the business shifted toward better inventory mixes and low-touch consignment programs, although selected seller programs added volume pressure.

Inventory Overhang Pressures Recovery

A major inventory cleanout by a top-10 retail client exceeded near-term buyer demand in some categories. That reduced recovery rates and increased storage, logistics, handling and receiving costs, leading the company to defer some sales.

Retail Pressure Expected to Ease

Elevated inventory from selected client flows is expected to weigh temporarily on recovery levels and first-quarter retail results. Management expects inventory conditions and recovery rates to normalize over the next few quarters.

Used-Vehicle Pricing Remains Soft

GovDeals’ fourth-quarter growth was partly offset by lower average vehicle values than a year earlier. Management expects vehicle pricing to remain softer in fiscal first-quarter 2027.

CAG Project Timing Affects GMV

CAG full-year GMV declined 2% to $245.2 million as several large EMEA projects moved into the first quarter and other international work was delayed. Management said project timing and a pause in some retail sales helped leave fourth-quarter GMV below its guidance range, although deferred transactions remain in the pipeline.

Fiscal First-Quarter Guidance

Management expects fiscal first-quarter 2027 GMV of $580 million to $640 million, adjusted EBITDA of $19 million to $22 million and GAAP net income of $8 million to $11 million. GAAP diluted EPS is projected at $0.24 to $0.33, adjusted diluted EPS at $0.36 to $0.45, and the effective tax rate at about 30%.

Growth Outlook and CAG Pipeline

Management described Liquidity Services as a double-digit organic growth business excluding acquisitions, both in the first quarter and for the year. CAG is expected to have a strong quarter as projects contracted during fiscal 2026, including work shifted from the fourth quarter, move toward completion.

Marketplace and Software Synergies

Management sees opportunities to connect Invaluable with AuctionZip, GovDeals, AllSurplus and Machinio by directing high-value assets to specialized buyers. AuctionZip’s roughly 30 million annual unique visitors also provide a potential base for expanding from an advertising marketplace into transactional auctions.

Acquisition Impact and GAAP Timing

Management expects Invaluable to add to adjusted net income and adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2027, including the first quarter, and to be accretive to full-year GAAP net income. Integration costs should be modest, but amortization and integration timing may cause quarterly GAAP results to vary.

Liquidity Services enters fiscal 2027 with record GMV, expanding margins, a debt-free balance sheet and a larger marketplace following the Invaluable deal. Although retail inventory pressure, vehicle pricing and project timing create near-term uncertainty, management’s growth outlook and technology investments kept the earnings call firmly constructive.

data.title: Harbor Diversified Delays Its Quarterly Report Filing
data.description:
Harbor BioSciences ( (HRBR) ) has released a notification of late filing.

Harbor Diversified, Inc. filed Form 12b-25 (Notification of Late Filing) for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. The delayed report is its Form 10-Q (Quarter Report), which the company says it could not complete by the prescribed deadline without unreasonable effort or expense.

The company and its independent registered public accounting firm devoted considerable time and resources to financial statement preparation, audit and review work. That work covered the company’s Form 10-K (Yearly Report) for 2025 and several earlier Form 10-Q (Quarter Report) filings, while resources were also directed toward the sale and disposition of its aviation assets.

Harbor Diversified does not expect to file the Form 10-Q (Quarter Report) within the five-day extension available under the late-filing rule. The notification does not provide a specific new filing date, so investors have not been given a firm timeline for the delayed report.

The company anticipates significant changes in its financial condition and results of operations compared with historical periods. After the aviation disposition, it says it has no material operating assets, is not engaged in an operating business, and has no source of revenue from operations; no quantitative preliminary results were provided.

The filing also states that the Form 10-Q (Quarter Report) filings for the quarters ended March 31, 2026, and June 30, 2026, remained outstanding. Harbor Diversified cautions that statements about the expected filing timing are forward-looking and could differ because of risks and uncertainties; the notification was signed by Chief Executive Officer and Secretary Christine R. Deister on November 20, 2026.

data.title: Red Robin’s Refranchising Strategy Raises Reliance on Royalties and Lease Risks
data.description:
Red Robin Gourmet Burgers (RRGB) has disclosed a new risk, in the Sales & Marketing category.

Red Robin’s recent refranchising has materially increased its dependence on franchise royalty income and the operational execution of franchisees, over whom it has reduced direct control. This shift heightens the risk that underperformance by franchise operators, or difficulties adapting the company’s cost structure to the evolving model, could adversely affect overall financial results.

In addition, Red Robin has retained lease and sublease obligations and other contractual commitments that could trigger payments if franchisees default or disputes arise. Any unexpected liabilities, post-closing claims, or failure to realize anticipated refranchising benefits could materially harm its business, financial condition, operating results, and cash flows.

This dynamic could materially pressure earnings, reduce free cash flow available for growth initiatives, and limit strategic flexibility in capital allocation.
